_why: IMPLEMENTATION of #1994, following the Stage-1 analysis merged as PR #2021 (.agents/tasks/1994-analysis.md on master). HAVING's raw input columns inside aggregate arguments are never bound at plan time and fall to per-record name resolution. The mechanism to fix it ALREADY EXISTS — rewrite_having_aggregate_arguments draws the source/output schema boundary at exactly the right depth and covers the compound-CASE case — but it has exactly ONE caller, inside visit_node, on predicate.clone(), for the completeness gate's coverage derivation, and its result is DISCARDED. It never reaches the executed plan. That is precisely the gated-additive-helper-with-no-production-caller anti-pattern the repo's production-wiring discipline forbids. Promotion converts dead diagnostic work into the executed plan. The analysis left R1 (sequencing vs #1747's index divergence) and R2 (a coupled pre-existing defect) as maintainer decisions; both are now PINNED in the brief — R1 as promote-with-names, R2 as out-of-scope and already filed as #2026.

anchors._note: the two-schema rewrite to promote. Today: one caller, on a clone, result discarded.
how the walker recognises a Filter as a HAVING and recovers the SOURCE schema + alias ctx. The main pass needs the same recognition — this is the reuse point, do not write a second one.

the main rewriter. Its Filter arm rewrites the predicate against input.schema (= the Aggregate's OUTPUT schema for a HAVING). The promotion lands HERE, not in the Aggregate arm — PlanNode::Aggregate has no `having` field.

blast_radius._note: 20 refs / 3 files, but most are the function's own internal recursion through BinaryOp/UnaryOp/Case/Between/InList arms. The external surface is ONE call site.

grammar_reference._note: §1c condition 2 carves HAVING out explicitly and MUST be amended in this PR (R3). Clause order post-#1962: SELECT -> FROM -> JOIN -> WHERE -> WINDOW -> GROUP BY -> HAVING -> ORDER BY -> LIMIT.

tests._note: fail_to_pass name is indicative — what is REQUIRED is a test proving a raw input column nested in a HAVING aggregate argument is bound at plan time after the change and was not before. Verify it FAILS pre-change. pass_to_stay includes the strict-gate test that proves the position is already consulted with the source schema — it must not regress.
